title: Tenure-Track Position in Public Policy and Governance – Department of Political Science and Global Development Studies
employer: Saint Mary's University - Faculty Employment Opportunities
description: Date Posted: September 11, 2026 Application Deadline: November 1, 2026 Department: Political Science and Global Development Studies Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time Group Affiliation: SMUFU, Rank of Assistant Professor Applications are invited for a probationary, tenure-track position in Public Policy and Governance at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning July 1, 2027. Applicants should hold a completed or nearly completed PhD in Political Science or Public Administration and have a demonstrable commitment to the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion as it pertains to service, teaching, and research. In support of the University's commitment to a diversified professoriate and in accordance with the University Employment Equity and Diversity policy, preference will be given to scholars who identify as Indigenous, Black or racialized. All applicants will be asked to complete and return a mandatory faculty self-identification form as part of the recruitment process. Indigenous applicants are required to document their Indigenous identity in their application and should be aware that the University may verify the community connections of applicants. We seek highly qualified applicants who can enrich our program with research and teaching excellence in the field of Public Policy and Governance. We are particularly interested in scholars who employ comparative politics methodologies and engage critically with structures of power and inequality. While the area of research expertise for this position is open, consideration will be given to applicants with expertise in one or more of the following areas: 1) Environmental justice and resource management; 2) Politics of representation, party politics and governing; 3) Inter-provincial politics and/or Crown-Indigenous governance in Canada; and 4) Social policy and public healthcare governance. The successful candidate must demonstrate a capacity to teach our existing Public Policy and Public Administration courses, as well as to develop new course offerings in the field of Public Policy and Governance. We also welcome candidates who demonstrate an interest in, or capacity for, providing students with experiential learning opportunities, such as community-engaged learning or practice-based projects connecting political science concepts to real-world contexts. Application Details At Saint Mary's University equity and diversity are integral to excellence and enrich our community. As an institution committed to fostering an environment of inclusion and respect, we welcome applications from women, Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/visible minorities, persons with disabilities, persons of minority sexual orientation or gender identity and others who might contribute to the growth and enrichment of our community. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents. If you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please contact hr@smu.ca. Teaching loads, employee benefits, and salary scales are governed by the Saint Mary's University Collective Agreement: https://www.smufu.ca/. All positions are subject to budgetary approval. Applications should consist of the following (7) items merged into ONE file: 1) application form (application form link); 2) cover letter describing how the candidate's areas of teaching and research expertise are relevant to the position; 3) curriculum vitae; 4) complete teaching dossier including teaching philosophy, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and relevant sample syllabi; 5) statement of research interests; 6) one piece of published or ongoing research, as well as links to other papers; and 7) names and contact information of three academic referees. Candidates may also include a statement detailing career interruptions or other special circumstances relevant to their applications (one page, maximum). This statement is optional. The closing date for applications is 11:59 pm (Atlantic time), Sunday November 1, 2026 Complete digital application files should be addressed to Dr. L. Zhyznomirska, Chairperson, and submitted at poli-gds@smu.ca. Lyubov Zhyznomirska, Chairperson Political Science and Global Development Studies Saint Mary's University EMAIL: poli-gds@smu.ca For any questions about the position or the application process, please contact the Chairperson at: chair.poligds@smu.ca.

title: Business Analyst
description:
Business Analyst

Eastlink

Work Location: 33 Alderney Drive, Dartmouth, NS (On-site, 5 days per week)

Department: Customer Care

Reports To: Director, Customer Service & Accounts Receivable

Employment Status: Full time, 40 hours per week

At Eastlink, our Business Analysts are driven by curiosity, problem-solving, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. By transforming data into actionable insights, they help us improve performance and enhance the customer experience to move the business forward.

In this role, you'll support our Customer Care and Accounts Receivable teams by providing analysis that helps leaders understand performance and anticipate future business needs. You'll work across teams to evaluate trends, support planning activities, and recommend improvements that contribute to operational effectiveness and business success.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Business Analyst, you'll help the business better understand performance, identify opportunities, and make informed decisions. You will:

• Monitor and analyze key operational, customer service, and Accounts Receivable metrics.

• Create and maintain reports, dashboards, and performance scorecards.

• Present findings in a clear way to help teams prioritize actions and achieve results.

• Support forecasting, workforce planning, and sales performance tracking.

• Partner with leaders to evaluate challenges, answer business questions, and recommend solutions.

• Contribute to improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency and support business goals.

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys working with information, asking thoughtful questions, and finding practical solutions. You’ll succeed in this role if you:

• Are naturally curious and enjoy understanding the story behind the numbers.

• Take ownership of your work and can confidently manage priorities independently.

• Approach challenges with strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.

• Can identify trends, evaluate impacts, and make well-supported recommendations.

• Are comfortable working with both detailed information and the bigger business picture.

• Build strong working relationships and collaborate effectively with different teams.

• Communicate clearly and can adjust information to different audiences.

• Have a strong commitment to accuracy, quality, and continuous learning.

What You’ll Bring

• Three or more years of experience in an analytical, financial, operational, or business support role.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience working with large and complex datasets.

• Demonstrated experience gathering, analyzing, and interpreting business data.

• Strong reporting and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate findings effectively.

• Experience working with performance metrics, forecasting, and operational reporting.

• Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and time management abilities.

• Experience with business intelligence, analytics, or data visualization tools.

• A results-oriented mindset and a desire to contribute to team and organizational success.

• Post-secondary education in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Analytics, or a related field, is considered an asset.

• Experience in a customer service, collections, call centre, or telecommunications environment is considered an asset.

About Eastlink

Eastlink is proudly family-owned and headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. After more than 50 years, we’ve grown from a small-town startup into one of Canada’s Best Managed companies without losing our entrepreneurial edge. We move fast. We try new things. We care about doing right by our customers, and we’re not afraid to take a different approach to make that happen.

Why Work with Us

We could say we’re not your typical telecom, but what makes us different is how we operate day to day. At Eastlink, we’re a tight-knit team all working toward common goals. We’re big enough to do meaningful work, but small enough that you can actually make your mark. You won’t get stuck waiting for layers of approval or years of tenure to make an impact! We believe in getting involved, speaking up, and figuring things out together. We’re always listening, learning, and adapting because our customers (and our people) expect us to. And just like we invest in our network, we invest in you, with intention and for the long run.

At the Department of Public Works, we are responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable provincial infrastructure for Nova Scotians. From highways and bridges to government buildings and registration of vehicles, safety and quality of life are top of mind. We support Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries.

Our Fleet Services Division is pivotal in ensuring the Public Works Fleet is running smoothly; ensuring the safety of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
As the Mobile Service Mechanic, you will have the opportunity to work on our wide variety of equipment that maintains our roads and highways. You will be responsible for maintaining Utility Tractors, Rubber Tire Loaders, Graders, Tandem Trucks and all associated attachments including wings, plows, and sweepers.

Primary Accountabilities
You will not only repair, rebuild and make adjustments to our fleet, but also determine the reasoning for equipment malfunctions. To minimize such occurrences, preventative maintenance is a critical component in this role.
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Your coveralls and other personal protective equipment (PPE) are provided. We also have an annual footwear and tool reimbursement allowance as you must bring your own mechanical tools.

Qualifications and Experience
Some high school and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport plus a minimum of five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience.

Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

A valid Class 5 drivers' license is a condition of employment, and an acceptable driver abstract must be submitted before employment begins. Air Brake endorsement is an asset.

Knowledge and experience of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology, electrical schematics, dealer purchased engine programs, online service manuals, and safety inspections are considered assets.

Air Conditioning Certification and a Motor Vehicle Inspection license would also be considered assets.

You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required.

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.

Normal hours of work are 8am - 4:30pm. If equipment breaks down, we will count on you to help things get up and running again. Therefore, you will be on-call outside of your regular work schedule.

This opportunity is for a 52-week Year-Round position – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

You must bring your own mechanical tools.

Building and maintaining our provincial infrastructure is no small job. We're recruiting for people like you to help our province achieve big things.
The Department of Public Works supports Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries. There are a lot of exciting developments on the horizon in our Province, and this is your opportunity to get involved with supporting the efficient flow of communications pertaining to summer and winter road construction, snow and ice control activities, and maintenance operations.

As the Baseperson I, you are responsible for the effective flow of communications within a geographic area of the province; ensuring the efficient dispatch of human, material, and equipment resources pertaining to snow and ice control activities and highway maintenance/operations.
You receive and record incoming calls and activities at the local maintenance base and provide general information with regards to Department policies. You provide top notch customer service and aid in resolving customer inquiries and concerns.

Primary Accountabilities
You are responsible for monitoring weather conditions and updating the electronic Road Condition Reporting System (511) on a regular basis. You maintain daily log records of all winter maintenance activities including equipment status, operator hours of work, material payloads from weigh scales, weather conditions, etc. You ensure equipment operators are dispatched to proper plow routes and support them by providing information and monitoring locations through radio contact and AVL technology. You are also a key contact in supporting Supervisor(s) by reporting equipment breakdowns and initiating emergency response procedures as required. General maintenance/organization of the base and light janitorial duties are required at times.
The successful candidate may also be required to perform the duties of other job positions as outlined in Group I of the CUPE Collective Agreement for which they are qualified.

Qualifications and Experience
Some High School and two (2) years of related experience in a dispatch or customer experience environment; an acceptable equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
You have experience around heavy equipment and construction, including the use of TMR/operational radio systems.
You are familiar with computer applications including Windows, internet, word processing, spreadsheets, data entry and email applications. Knowledge of the geographical area is required to respond effectively to staff and public inquiries, and to respond appropriately in emergency response situations.
Training or certification in the following subject areas are considered assets: SAP, WHMIS, First Aid and CPR, Transportation of Dangerous Goods, and knowledge of department policies and procedures.
You are a self-motivated individual who works independently with minimal supervision and participates fully as an effective team player.
You are accurate in your work, have a mathematical aptitude, and have well developed time management and organizational skills to meet established deadlines and priorities. You have strong communication skills, along with a strong customer service focus.
